trust_decision.summary: Workspace paths supplied through the global config or the Pipeline step must contain no parent-directory (`..`) segment and must stay below the Disk/mount point; at the pinned commit the only decision made anywhere is relativeness, and `..` passes every one of those checks, in the descriptor validators and again at allocation time.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary only says 'path traversal'; a grep for path validation lands on the plugin's single workspace-path validator, which checks only that the value is relative. That same function also backs the `path` field of the exwsAllocate step (ExwsAllocateStep.java:123-125), so it is the first place an engineer reads.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /descriptorByName/org.jenkinsci.plugins.ewm.definitions.DiskPool/doCheckWorkspaceTemplate and POST /descriptorByName/org.jenkinsci.plugins.ewm.steps.ExwsAllocateStep/doCheckPath (both call validateWorkspaceTemplate, DiskPool.java:109-111 and ExwsAllocateStep.java:123-125)
POST /descriptorByName/org.jenkinsci.plugins.ewm.definitions.Disk/doCheckPhysicalPathOnDisk (physicalPathOnDisk field of the Disk config form, Disk/config.jelly:12-14)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The compute* methods are allocation-time plumbing, and their inputs were already checked by the descriptor doCheck* handlers when the value was entered in a form, so re-checking `..` here reads as redundant defensive code rather than part of the fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Job/folder names are appended verbatim, so a path segment may legitimately contain two consecutive dots as part of a name (e.g. a job named `release..final` given template `${JOB_NAME}/${BUILD_NUMBER}`); a fix that rejects the substring `..` instead of a whole `..` segment breaks those valid workspaces, and rejecting the empty physicalPathOnDisk also breaks the supported 'path is just JOB_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER' layout.

O6_input_shapes: `..` as a whole segment at the start (`../x`), in the middle (`a/../../x`) and at the end (`x/..`)
Windows-style separators (`..\\x`), which hudson.Util.isRelativePath also treats as relative
the value produced after `Util.replaceMacro` expansion of a template, e.g. `${CUSTOM_BUILD_PARAM}` resolving to `..` (ExwsAllocateExecution.java:270)
a `..` substring inside one legitimate segment (job name `release..final`), which an over-broad check would wrongly reject
omitted/empty physicalPathOnDisk, which is legitimate and must keep working (ExwsAllocateStepTest.java:104-112)

O7_producer.where: src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/ewm/steps/ExwsAllocateStep.java:105-109 (configure binds the diskPools JSON straight into DiskPool objects and saves; the same objects are built by JCasC, src/test/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/ewm/casc/ConfigAsCodeTest.java:38-53), and the path itself is produced later at allocation time in ExwsAllocateExecution.java:243-285

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Pipeline `exwsAllocate path: '../..'` reaches computeCustomPath at build time, which tests only isRelativePath and leftover `${`, so the `..` path becomes the workspace FilePath handed to the nested steps (ExwsExecution.java:103-104).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The identical value is checked by doCheckPath/validateWorkspaceTemplate in the snippet generator, so the runtime method looks like it can rely on that validation; only a hand-written Jenkinsfile bypasses it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file in the same steps/ package as the allocation code, but a different route from the validator in utils/

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Global `Workspace path template` is re-resolved at allocation time in computePathBasedOnTemplate with only an isRelativePath test, so a template persisted through config.xml or JCasC (which never call doCheckWorkspaceTemplate) keeps `..` and escapes the disk.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The template field is validated in the global config form and config.xml/JCasC are trusted admin surfaces, so allocation-time re-validation looks unnecessary.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: steps/ vs utils/ and definitions/ (2 packages, 2 files)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Disk.physicalPathOnDisk is appended to JOB_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER in computeDefaultPathOnDisk with only an isRelativePath test, and its own validator (Disk.doCheckPhysicalPathOnDisk) has the same gap.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is an admin-only global-config field that already has a dedicated form validator, so it looks like the safer of the three path sources.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: definitions/ validator and steps/ runtime method, 2 packages from utils/

O8_uncovered_routes.route: An allocated ExternalWorkspace.pathOnDisk is persisted (run action ExwsAllocateActionImpl.java:23 + run.save() at ExwsAllocateExecution.java:150, fingerprint facet at :166-175), reused unchecked by a downstream job (:114-132) and browsed through /exws/browse/<id>/ws/ (ExternalWorkspace.java:87-97); a path stored before the fix or through any unguarded route stays traversable across reload.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The workspace was validated when it was first allocated, and a downstream job reusing an existing allocation is a neighbouring feature, so re-validating persisted state looks out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: model/ plus actions/ and the fingerprint facet, 3 packages from utils/

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fourth path source next to computeCustomPath/computePathBasedOnTemplate/computeDefaultPathOnDisk that mints a workspace path (for example a per-node override or a resolved `path` setter).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every workspace path in the plugin is manufactured in this class and every new path option has to add a compute* method here; a maintainer adding a per-node path override would naturally put it beside the existing three.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A workspace-path/template field on Template, mirroring DiskPool.workspaceTemplate, bound from the same External Workspace Templates global config.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Template already mirrors DiskPool's disk definitions and is bound from the same global form (ExwsStep.java:61-65); adding a template-level workspace path is a natural feature and would need the same parent-segment rejection.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second construction/deserialization route into ExternalWorkspace (a readResolve or legacy-migration constructor) that accepts a persisted pathOnDisk.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already crosses the serialization boundary (RunAction2 and FingerprintFacet) and the plugin keeps compatibility readResolve code elsewhere (NodeDisk.java:39-44), so a migration path accepting legacy stored paths is plausible.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22): a relative path with parent-directory segments reaches filesystem sinks (workspace allocation, FilePath.child, workspace browser) without canonicalisation against the disk/mount point
